pick.reason: It is the only rough that stays on brand (white, black, one red) and holds up at both sizes, and it needs the fewest notes to get there: the split on linkedin, the stack on ig-post, and the crank is the one red thing to look at.
pick.lost: 2 uses a black background, which breaks the brand's white-and-black rule, puts the copy in a box inside a box, and crops the crank at the edge until it reads as a blob; 3 has a strong linkedin, but its ig-post drops the headline to the single word "bedroom." and leaves an empty band of about 850px, which is a composition fault under the standard.
notes: linkedin: widen the left text column to 55% (660px), and set the headline from about 52px to 61px on the brand scale, line height 1.05, tracking -0.02em. A 2-line or 3-line wrap is fine (standard: headline at least 7% of the short side, no more than 3 lines on landscape).
ig-post: headline from about 85px to 95px, line height 1.0, tracking -0.02em, and let it wrap to 3 lines. Keep the supporting line at 31px with a 32px gap under the headline.

ig-post: rotate the crank -24deg to match linkedin, and scale it until the arm spans the grey panel's width minus 64px on each side. Right now it sits as a small flat bar in a big grey field. The panel should hold one diagonal shape, not leftover air (standard: air is deliberate when it is shaped).
ig-post: end the grey panel at y=1215 so the 10% bottom safe zone (135px) stays white, and keep its 64px side margins. Leave the mark at top left, 20px, 400 weight, foreground.
linkedin: move the crank's centre to x=930, y=330 in the right-hand grey panel, and scale it so the far end sits 56px inside the right edge. Both ends stay inside the panel with no edge contact.

hierarchy: linkedin: the red crank reads before the 61px headline. Set the headline to 76px, 700, line height 1.05, tracking -0.02em, so it wraps to 3 lines inside the 660px column. Keep the supporting line 32px under it and the block's bottom at y=587.

typography: on both sizes, break the headline after the comma as "A bike crank, / from a spare / bedroom." Linkedin currently strands "a" at the end of line 1 and splits the phrase. Use a
after "crank," and keep "spare bedroom." together with a non-breaking space only if the 3-line wrap allows it.

composition: ig-post: the inset grey panel reads as a box inside a box. Bleed it to x=0 and x=1080, keeping y=559 to 1215. Leave the crank at its current size and position (ends at x=128 and x=952) so the panel matches linkedin's full-bleed right half.

originality: the crank is a generic rounded bar with a dot. Make it a real part. Replace the white ring and black dot at the spindle end with one 56px square bore, radius 2, fill #0a0a0a, rotated with the arm, to read as a square-taper spindle. Keep the pedal-end hole round, 40px, fill #f2f2f2. Same change on both sizes.
brand: the mark is about 22px on linkedin and 20px on ig-post. Set it to 20px, 400, #0a0a0a on both, top left at the safe-zone corner (40px on linkedin, 64px on ig-post).
polish: linkedin: once the headline is 76px, check that the gap between the mark and the headline is no less than 96px. If it is, drop the headline block to start at y=320.

notes: composition: on ig-post, bleed the grey panel to y=1350 so there is no 135px white strip under it. Keep the crank's lowest point at or above y=1215. Scale the crank so it spans x=64 to x=1016 (it is now about 128 to 952), still at -24deg.

hierarchy: on ig-post, the red crank reads before the headline. Take the headline from 95px to 119px (line height 1.0, tracking -0.02em, still 3 lines, "A bike crank," about 720px wide) so the type block carries the top and matches the figure's mass. Start the panel at y=632.

typography: on ig-post, keep the supporting line at 31px with a 32px gap under the 119px headline. On linkedin, keep the headline at 76px and 3 lines. Sizes per artboard stay at three: 119/31/20 on ig-post and 76/25/20 on linkedin.
spacing: on linkedin, lift the whole headline block 8px so the supporting line's descenders sit about 52px off the bottom edge, matching the mark's top inset. Keep the 40px headline-to-support gap.

originality: on both sizes, give the crank a hard-edged shoulder where the arm meets each boss (a straight 2px-radius step, not a smooth blend), so it reads as machined aluminium, not a generic paddle. Keep the black square spindle and the white pedal eye.
polish: on linkedin, nudge the crank centre up 16px to y=314 so its top end lines up with the headline's first-line cap height.

notes: originality: the split is pattern 1 as written. Let the crank cross the split to make the move only this card makes. composition: on linkedin the crank fills only about 250px of the panel's 627px height, so about 200px of grey above it and 170px below is leftover. hierarchy: on ig-post the red crank, about 950x550px, reads before the 119px headline. Keep the headline at 119px and move the grey panel's top from y=632 to y=664, so 96px of white sits under the supporting line and the headline group reads first and as one block.

typography: on linkedin the supporting line measures about 23px, under the 24px card minimum. Set it to 25px (brand scale). Set the mark to 20px on both sizes (it measures about 18px now). Keep the headline at 76px on linkedin and 119px on ig-post, both 700, line height 1.05, tracking -0.02em.

spacing: the linkedin outer margins are uneven (40px left, about 45px top, about 55px bottom). Set all of them to 40px: mark top at y=40, left edge x=40, supporting line's text box ending at y=587. Keep the headline to supporting line gap at 48px on both sizes.
